summary: Tuscaloosa County steel lookout dedicated in 1940 to H.E. Westervelt; sources conflict on the first wooden tower, and its current condition is unverified.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower (NHLR); a 1966 report describes a wooden tower built in 1940
facts.status_note: The NHLR entry has no removal date, but no source read confirms a tower standing today; a 1966 report says a wooden tower at the site was destroyed in a tornado

events.note: NHLR says the steel tower was built circa 1940 to replace a wooden tower that burned; the 1966 Tuscaloosa News item says the wooden tower was built in 1940. The sources conflict on which tower dates to 1940
Dedicated in July 1940 to Herbert E. Westervelt, founder of Gulf States Paper

Tuscaloosa News item dated March 5, 1966, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page: the Westervelt tower at Buhl is listed among towers destroyed in a tornado; the same report says the wooden tower was lifted off its foundation
Same report says plans were already under way to replace the Westervelt tower with a steel structure

evidence.supports: Steel tower built circa 1940 to replace a wooden tower which burned
evidence.quote: This 100-foot steel tower was built in circa 1940 to replace a previous wooden tower which burned.

evidence.supports: Dedicated to Herbert E. Westervelt in July 1940
evidence.quote: The tower was dedicated to Herbert E. Westervelt, founder of Gulf States Paper (now the Westervelt Company), in July 1940.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
Forest Lookouts page has a Pickens County heading over the Westervelt entry
Report is a Tuscaloosa News item

evidence.quote: Timber damage in Thursday night's tornado

evidence.supports: Wooden tower built in 1940 and dedicated to H.E. Westervelt
evidence.quote: The wooden tower was built in 1940 and dedicated to H.E. Westervelt

evidence.quote: The old wooden tower was lifted completely off of its foundation.

evidence.supports: Guide wires kept the tower from being blown away

evidence.quote: Plans were already under way to replace the Westervelt Tower with a steel structure

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR places the tower in Tuscaloosa County, which matches the brief's coordinates. The Forest Lookouts page's Pickens County heading sits over a 1966 report that also names the Grove Tower at Benevola in Pickens County, so the heading may refer to that tower. Tuscaloosa County is used.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. The sources conflict on the 1940 build and on what ended the first wooden tower: NHLR says it burned before the steel tower went up, while the 1966 Tuscaloosa News item, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, says a tornado destroyed a wooden 1940 tower. The brief's 'standing' status is not confirmed by any source read; this record uses 'unverified'. The 1966 report mentions a planned steel replacement, which could be the NHLR steel tower, but that is unconfirmed. A separate unnamed tower on Yellow Creek Road north of Tuscaloosa turned up in search results; nothing links it to this record, so it is not used. Access is unknown and is omitted.
